sanskrit_verse: अशक्तप्रेतनष्टेषु क्षेत्रिकेष्वनिवारितः । क्षेत्रं चेद्विकृषेत् कश्चिदश्नुवीत स तत्फलम् ॥
transliteration: aśaktapretanaṣṭeṣu kṣetrikeṣv anivāritaḥ | kṣetraṃ ced vikṛṣet kaścid aśnuvīta sa tatphalam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When the owner of the field is incapacitated, deceased, or otherwise unable to act, and another cultivates the land, that person becomes entitled to its fruits.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from active engagement, not passive ownership
Causation aligns with conscious participation in creation
Restoration logic honors productive effort over nominal claim
Consciousness alignment recognizes the doer as the enjoyer
executable_legal_axioms: IF landowner is incapacitated OR deceased AND another individual cultivates the land, THEN entitlement transfers to the cultivator
IF no active cultivation occurs by the nominal owner, THEN no passive entitlement to produce is valid
IF a person performs the causal action of cultivation, THEN that person assumes rightful enjoyment of the fruit
ENTITLEMENT is determined by capacity-in-action, not by positional authority alone
supreme_court_application: In adjudication involving property rights where ownership is nominal but cultivation or stewardship is active, the threshold of responsibility lies in operational causality. The Supreme Court must recognize that entitlement follows the one whose conscious capacity sustains production, thereby aligning jurisprudence with dharma-rooted causality rather than static ownership claims.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causality flows from the active engagement of cultivation. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that the sequence of sowing, tending, and harvesting belongs to the cultivator. Responsibility is proportional to contribution. There is no punishment; there is recognition of factual alignment between cause and consequence within consciousness.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Recognize the cultivator's labor as the operative cause of yield
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Nominal owner must acknowledge lapse in duty
Capacity Restoration: Realign ownership structures to reflect active engagement
Integrity Reintegration: Ensure all parties honor the causal truth of production
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law: Entitlement arises from conscious causation. Dharma is restored through recognition of the cultivator’s rightful claim. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
